# Lidlit

> Lidlit is a free macOS menu bar app that controls the glowing Apple logo on the lid of a MacBook Pro XDR. It turns the lid light into a quiet status light: a steady glow, a slow breathe, or a blink when Claude, ChatGPT, email or chat needs you. Website: https://lidlit.app (formerly Lidlight, lidlight.app).

- Download (free, 1.6 MB DMG): https://github.com/Lafsen/lidlit-site/releases/latest/download/Lidlit.dmg
- Requirements: MacBook Pro XDR with a lit logo, macOS 14 or later, Apple silicon.
- Not on the Mac App Store: the App Store doesn't allow apps that drive the logo light. It isn't notarized yet, so on first launch open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.
- Price: free. Optional tips: https://lidlit.app/support/
- Not affiliated with Apple.

## What it does

- Modes: Steady (fixed brightness), Breathe (slow fade in and out, adjustable speed), Follow (tracks the screen brightness), or off.
- Auto-dim: softer in a dark room, using the Mac's light sensor.
- Notifications: blinks in a distinct rhythm when Claude Code or Codex (ChatGPT) finishes or needs input (installs their hooks with one switch), and for new email (Mail, Outlook, Spark and others) and chat messages (Slack, Teams, Messages, WhatsApp, Discord, Telegram), read from the unread badge on the app's Dock icon.
- Morse code: type a message and the lid spells it out; saved messages can be used as a notification's signal.
- Schedule: different behaviour at different times of day.
- Lid closed: can keep glowing, or only flash for notifications, while you use an external display.
- Scripting: `lidlit cue <name>`, `lidlit level 0-100`, `lidlit mode steady|breathe|followScreen|off`, and a `lidlit://` URL scheme for Shortcuts.

## Common questions

- CPU: 0.0 % at rest; while breathing, macOS does the fading itself (about 2 % in its own brightness service).
- Battery: the app barely does anything; the LED uses a little power, less at lower brightness.
- Color: no. The logo has a single white light, so signals use rhythm instead.
- Privacy: it never reads email or message contents, only Dock badge counts for apps you turn on. Nothing leaves the Mac.
- Undo: Reset hands the light back to macOS.
